summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, prior stents, diabetes, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for chest pain concerning for unstable angina. Initial evaluation showed no myocardial infarction, with normal troponins and ECG. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which revealed significant diffuse disease in the LAD artery. He successfully underwent percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA) of the LAD without stent placement. He remained chest pain-free post-procedure, with stable vital signs and improved renal function. His home medications, including dual antiplatelet therapy, statin, beta-blocker, and antihypertensives, were continued. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up instructions for cardiology and primary care, and guidance on medication adherence and symptom monitoring.
